facts.raw_span: A 74-year-old Caucasian woman
chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis
treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution
grade 4 neutropenia (<500/μL) for over 15 days
febrile peak
tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs
lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core
severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with minimal necrosis, angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching were seen, along with numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa
A 74-year-old Caucasian woman
chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis
treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution

febrile peak

severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with minimal necrosis, angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching were seen, along with numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, are consistent with mucormycosis, a rare but serious fungal infection.

The patient's grade 4 neutropenia and febrile peak, along with the development of skin lesions, could be consistent with aspergillosis, a fungal infection that can occur in immunocompromised individuals.
The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core could be consistent with cutaneous candidiasis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions.

The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation, could be consistent with blastomycosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions.
The patient's grade 4 neutropenia and febrile peak could be consistent with histoplasmosis, a fungal infection that can occur in immunocompromised individuals.
The patient's grade 4 neutropenia and febrile peak could be consistent with cryptococcosis, a fungal infection that can occur in immunocompromised individuals.

The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation, could be consistent with scedosporiosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions.
The patient's grade 4 neutropenia and febrile peak could be consistent with fusariosis, a fungal infection that can occur in immunocompromised individuals.

The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation, could be consistent with phaeohyphomycosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions.

The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation, could be consistent with basidiobolomycosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions.
